children: Starting next year, the Federal Open Market Committee will make policy decisions at seven meetings, not the usual eight, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said Wednesday after the Fed's decision to keep rates unchanged.
"Quashing inflation is not about a fixed calendar date," he said. Note that the Fed has always had the ability to adjust its rate outside the regular meeting dates.
In 2027, one meeting per year will focus on strategy without setting policy. That will likely change to two meetings in 2028, he said, implying only six policy decisions will be made.
Economic growth has strengthened, with Q3 GDP growth appearing to expand at over 3%. High tech is leading the growth. Other categories are also contributing, the Fed chair said.
On the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, the situation is positive, Warsh said.

"It's our responsibility to get inflation down," he said. We have started to see some changes in financial and credit conditions. Overall financial conditions are tighter but shouldn't be considered "tight," he said.
The FOMC is "concerned, but not surprised" by the volatility in markets.
It's the committee's job to make sure that "relative price changes in some sectors do not broaden out through the economy," Warsh said.

title: Fed policymakers to reduce number of policy-setting meetings next year: Warsh press conference
